report.source_text: Physical examination found small vesicles (1–2 mm diameter) surrounded by erythema had developed on his trunk and back (Fig. 1a) and on the neck (Supplementary Fig. S1A). These vesicles were diagnosed as varicella. The papules and vesicles in ribbons on the left ear involved 1 to 3 dermatomes, the vesicular eruption was unilateral, lesions appeared over the first 5 days, and they were ulcerated.

report.source_text: The viral load of VZV was assessed using real-time PCR [14], and the viral load of VZV in the head (mean of Ct = 17.35) was higher than that in the trunk (mean of Ct = 18.64) (Supplementary Fig. S2B).

clinician.final_diagnosis: infection with VZV genotype J causes a rare case of concurrent varicella and herpes zoster in an adult
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 44-year-old man presented with unilateral vesicular eruption and pain on the left ear involving 1 to 3 dermatomes and small vesicles on the trunk, back, and neck. Nested PCR testing confirmed VZV infection without HSV. Genotyping of viral DNA from lesions on head and trunk identified VZV genotype J. Physical examination differentiated herpes zoster lesions (left ear, unilateral, dermatomal, ulcerated) and varicella lesions (multiple small vesicles on trunk/neck). The patient was treated with valacyclovir and other supportive medications, with lesions crusting and resolving after 1 week. Viral load was higher in head lesions than trunk.
